src/application/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts: execute() creates the order with the domain factory createOrder(orderId, customerId, items).
src/application/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts: execute() saves through the abstract OrderRepository (this.orderRepository.save(order)) and contains no storage code itself.
src/application/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts: PlaceOrderRequest is a plain input type for the use case, with no transport or framework coupling.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: PlaceOrderUseCase.execute does the coordination work expected of an application-layer use case. It checks every item against the domain Catalog (getProduct, canReserve) before reserving any stock, then reserves stock through the domain (reserve), builds the order through the domain factory (createOrder), and saves it through the OrderRepository abstraction. The stock and availability decisions themselves stay in the domain Catalog; the use case only puts the steps in order so that nothing is reserved unless every item passes. The file has no persistence code, no transport or HTTP handling, and no framework logic. Generating an ID with Date.now() and Math.random() is a small concern, but placing it in the application layer is acceptable. It is not a business rule and not infrastructure code. No ADR prose was given to check against.
